Sunday to Monday: Snow and a localized rain/snow mix will 
expand across the early Sunday morning and continue into the 
early afternoon, before decreasing. However additional 
precipitation chances develop Sunday night into Monday AM. The 
center of an occluding low pressure system is off the coast and 
the deformation axis stretching from Oregon north and then 
northwest toward the offshore low will be main impetus for the 
precipitation. Snow was falling around the southern Cascades 
into the Wenatchee area Saturday evening and through Sunday 
Monday this precipitation expand throughout the Cascades, 
Waterville Plateau through the Upper Columbia Basin. Toward mid-
morning through midday precipitation expand over southeast WA 
and the Spokane/C'dA Area and central southern ID Panhandle. It 
progresses into northeast WA and north ID toward late morning to
early afternoon, while it starts to wane from the southwest. 
The boundary/deformation axis start to lose definition by mid 
to later afternoon to evening and the precipitation potential 
weakens. An additional wave moves in from the west overnight 
tonight into Monday AM, allowing for the redevelopment of the 
threat over the Cascades Sunday overnight and across all of 
central WA Monday before a brief lull that retreat the main snow
threat back against the Cascade crest.

For Sunday a wildcard for snow amounts is how any embedded mid-
level impulses work with any of the unstable mid-level lapse 
rates. Right now the that instability doesn't entirely sync with
the best lift. Yet if any outlying unresolved shortwaves 
combined with them it could bring locally enhanced 
precipitation rates. Snow is forecast to the predominant 
precipitation weather type, save for the deeper Columbia Basin 
and L-C Valley and possibly in the afternoon around places like 
Spokane Valley and the Palouse. The higher snow amounts around 1
to 3 inches are forecast around the Cascades to the Waterville 
Plateau, including the higher elevations around the Wenatchee 
Area. Winter weather advisories are in place for these areas 
through midday Sunday. Elsewhere where snow occurs amounts 
between 0.1" to 1.0" are possible, locally higher elevations of 
the northern WA and ID Panhandle mountains. That includes the 
potential for couple inches at Sherman and Lookout Pass. Snow 
around the Spokane/C'dA metro is that wide range, with the 
lowest amounts in the Spokane Valley/Downtown and higher toward
the western portions of Spokane County. That wildcard 
instability could locally enhance snowfall rates elsewhere, so 
that is something we will have to keep an eye on but confidence 
in that occurrence is low.

As we head into Sunday evening to Monday morning we will have to
watch for a few things. There will be the fog and freezing fog 
threat that will be over much of basin and valley areas. 
Additionally any snow that may have melted could also refreeze 
on road surfaces, so commuters will have to keep an eye on roads
for slick spots Monday morning. Highs will be in lower 30s to 
near 40 Sunday, warmest near the deeper basin and L-C Valley. 
Monday will see highs in the mid-40s to lower 40s. Lows will 
largely be in the 20s.

Tuesday to Saturday: The Inland Northwest remains in an active 
pattern, as system after system moves in from the Pacific. 
Temperature gradually warm through the week, with highs in the 
mid-30s to mid-40s Tuesday (coldest near the Cascades) pushing 
to mostly 40s by Thursday outside the mountains and the 30s in 
the mountains. Right now Tuesday and Thursday looks like the 
wettest days, with mountains snow and a lowland rain/snow mix 
Tuesday and mainly mountain snow and lowland rain Thursday. the 
most impactful precipitation will be the potential for some 
Moderate snow around the Cascade passes Tuesday with 2-5 inches.
Other snows will be possible over most passes Thursday, though 
Washington Pass is currently forecast to see the most with over 
6 inches possible; models show a 65-70% chance of 6" and 25% 
chance of up 12 inches. Most other passes are forecast to see 2 
inches or less Thursday. Meanwhile the lowlands could see some 
moderate rain Thursday, with a 50-70% chance for 0.25" of rain. 
Thursday is also forecast to be a breezy day, especially over 
the Columbia Basin/Spokane/C'dA Area and Palouse, with a 30-60%
chance of wind gusts over 30 mph and 15-30% chance of gusts 
over 40 mph. /Solveig
